Ordered the watermelon juice and the Al -Manzil Burger which came with a really nice BBQ sauce. Later on in the night I had another knock on the door, the hotel had sent me a gift. Again another example of the hotel staff going over and beyond. This hotel is a true star and really deserves to be recognised as a 4* Plus property with 5* services. What I liked was the personal service by the staff which is usually not found in larger 5* properties in Dubai.

title: what a hotel
text: stopped in many hotels around the world from 5 star to 2 star and this has got to be the best i have ever stayed in4 star hotel never 5 star + and it soon will be when the dubai tower and dubai mall are finishedcheck it out now before the 5 star prices start

title: Uniquely different despite developing location
text: My wife and I have always stayed at the Movenpick Hotel whenever we visit Dubai (we now live in Bahrain) and this is our first time at Al Manzil, as per recommendation by my boss. Whilst the location is nowhere near as good as Movenpick (as it sits between Wifi, Ramsey, various little shops and restaurants, and the airport) as Al Manzil situates in the middle of Dubai's development zone and takes an average of 30mins to go wherever you wants to go (e.g. airport, Mall of the Emirates, Gold Souk, Burj Al Arab, etc, etc); the room (open plan bathroom is unique), the decoration (mix of Middle Eastern with contemporary), the view from the room (Burj Dubai if you are lucky), the pool (a bit exposed though), the services (always with a smile) is streets ahead of Movenpick! So I guess it's up to you whether the location or room/service is your cup of tea...

title: Wow!!
text: Dubai is the home of bling so it's refreshing to see a hotel taking its own route! Al Manzil really stands out with a genuinely contemporary style that is imaginative, different and atmospheric.I guarantee you won't have ever stayed in a bedroom quite like it. Kind of open plan with a bathtub at the foot of your bed, flanked by various cubicles and a curvaceous TV stand full of drinkies and snacks. Very cute lighting that creates an instant mellow feel and a really beautiful vanity sink lit-up like a Moroccan lantern. It's really peachy.As a business hotel there were some issues. It is quite new so maybe they are still working it all out. Sorry to say the Dubai internet curse was in full flow. No wireless connection in the room at all during my time here. That's a serious problem. "Sorry Mister Soft the wireless is down". So I decamped to the business centre, which had working internet but a non-working printer. It got fixed but the duty manager clearly had zero knowledge or training in IT support.Only after leaving did my colleague casually mention that his room wireless worked fine throughout. Hmm, it was all a lie then.Anyway aside from that an absolutely splendid and quite beautifully styled hotel that would fit the bill perfectly for a groovy young couple or romantic getaway.

title: Great hotel in a developing area
text: Stayed at this hotel twice for business during April 2008. Love it. Stunning rooms, ultra modern with large flat screen TVs that you can watch from the bath if you wish. Lovely swimming pool. Is attached to a supermarket and a suk (small shopping centre). Fabulous restaurant where you can eat outside or inside with a la carte or delicious buffet. Breakfast is great. Service INCREDIBLE. The location is the old town which is actually a brand new area close to the Burj tower. 10 minute taxi ride to the business area (Sheikh Zayed Road) and about 25/30 mins to the beach.

title: Fantastic Hotel
text: We chose to stay in Al Manzil while in Dubai - having been in the Maldives for the first 9 nights of our holiday the beach wasnt a priority for this stay. The hotel is absolutely fantastic! The rooms are a good size with a king sized bed, a glass-enclosed bathtub, separate toilet and shower cubicle. Free bottles of water were given every day and there was also coffee and tea making facilities.The food was fabulous, a great selection of hot and cold choices at breakfast and dinner.The hotel isnt city centre but is only a short taxi drive from all the attractions.This hotel wouldnt be what it is without the staff  they are brilliant, so friendly and helpful and they couldnt do enough for you!

title: Fantastic hotel in the Old Town
text: I stayed in this hotel for a total of 5 nights at the end of a 2 month holiday in Europe. The hotel was absolutely beautiful. The staff were very friendly and would help in any way they could. The breakfast was more than adequate and the service outstanding. The bedroom was very spacious with an open plan bathroom with bathtub and a separate shower. The bed was very comfortable and turned down each night with a chocolate left on the pillow. I would definitely stay in this hotel again and would recommend it to anyone travelling to Dubai

title: Geatfun:)Loved it!!!
text: the stay was a very nice experience.its clean,tidy by all standadsa 4++++ hotel.its practical nice roomlayouting.great breakfast.the staff are really nice and helpful. i would definitely come back.i was there for business and it was a very fruitful trip thanks to all facilities here..

title: Loved the Al Manzil
text: We stayed for 5 days and found the all of the staff without exception to be very courteous and extremely helpful when called on. It was a pleasure and we would not hesitate to stay with them again or recommend Al Manzil to friends planning to visit Dubai. The breakfasts are awsome and the rooms modern and well appointed.

title: 4 Star!!? I Give This Fantastic Hotel A High 5.
text: I knew I made the right choice the minute I stepped into this hotel's Arabian-inspired lobby. I was given a refreshing cold apple drink and a cold towel while waiting to be checked in, and then shown to my room. It was big with a huge king size bed, a fantastic glass-enclosed bathtub, separate toilet and a separate shower cubicle. The amenities were top-notch and numerous and free bottles of water were replenished every day and there was also free coffee and tea facilities,as well as chocolate covered dates every night at turndown!!The swimming pool was also fantastic overlooking Burj Dubai, the tallest building in the world and the temperature was just right. I met with smiles at evry turn and really wished that my stay was longer than 2 nights.It just shows that 4 star hotels in Dubai beat most 5 star hotels in almost every other city, Dubai is overwhelming with its malls, buildings,nightlife etc and this wonderful hotel was a haven of tranquility in quite a wild city!

title: Style
text: Our tour operator (Friendly Planet) booked us into the Al Manzil Hotel. We were greeted with juice & coffee as we waited for our key. The staff went out of their way at every turn to make sure we had what we needed throughout our stay and were given help with our plans, including transportation to and from some of the malls. (Hazel was especially wonderful)The breakfast buffet, which was included, was fantastic, with local specialties, fruits & yogurts, waffles, omelettes, and many other hot and cold items. How about 6 types of juices, including mango or watermelon juice? And they served plenty of good coffee, that we Americans really needed to start our day. (although there is a Starbuck's adjacent if you are a serious coffee junkie)Our room was in perfect condition, and our view was of the neighborhood and some of the skyskrapers under construction. You might think looking out on construction is a bad thing, but it was fascinating, considering the size and scope of the project. Looking out on the world's tallest bulding is amazing! The design of the interior had a slight "W" hotel vibe to it, with an Arabic twist. The beds and pillows were very comfortable, and there was a great mini-bar, big flat-screen TV, writing desk, free internet service and robes and slippers. The glass-enclosed bathtub was more of a novelty for us, and the shower was a glass enclosure, as was the W.C. I wasn't sure I would enjoy this room design (when we previewed the hotel on the website) but we found it to be unique and enjoyable. Turn-down service included a chocolate covered almond-stuffed date and there was a complimentary plate of chocolate truffles when we arrived.The pool was small and quiet, and we were able to enjoy a cold beer or lunch brought to us there. We visited the beach hotels, and I found that they were more or less like going to Disneyworld. Huge, beautiful, but filled with tons of kids, and sunburned tourists, lots of shoppers, and they were just too crazy for me. I'd stay at the Al Manzil any time, and since taxi transportation is so inexpensive (and hotel shuttle service is free) I would choose this location again, even though the area is under construction. When the construction is complete, this hotel will probably be out of sight, price-wise, so stay there now, while you can afford it!

title: Love this hotel!
text: I loved everything about this hotel, the rooms are modern, big and comfortable, extremely clean and fresh; they have a beautiful outside area where people can eat, smoke shisha or just have a nice time out, also good selection of restaurants and a very good breakfast.The Business Centre is complete and they also have free internet access in every room, the staff is friendly and helpful and made my stay at the Al Manzil very pleasant, probably the location is not the best to know the city, this hotel is perfect for business people looking to relax after a long working day, I will definitely recommend it and would love to go again!

title: Good hotel for a short break but not near the beach
text: We stayed at the Al Manzil hotel as part of a two-centre holiday to the Maldives and Dubai. We spent 4 days here and really enjoyed our stay, although we didn't spend much time at the hotel itself. First off, the hotel is in the new area of "Downtown Burj Dubai". This is really hard to find on a map, cos it's so new and generally most of it is still under construction. It's near the World Trade Centre and Emirates Towers area of the city. Location wise, the hotel is well situated for a few days break in Dubai, as it is within a short taxi ride of all the major malls, beaches, sightseeing tours etc. (taxis are really cheap in Dubai). However, if you want to spend a lot of time at the beach, you'd be better off booking a hotel at the beach itself! The hotel itself is great. Good room, good food, great staff and we really enjoyed our stay. We didn't have time to use the pool, but it looked nice. The hotel is really geared mostly towards business travellers, but was fine for tourists.

title: Best hotel in Dubai
text: Still new and clean.... not worn out like some of the others... modern and arabic mixed together in lovely way. Bathtub in the middle of the room! Great food at the restaurants.... loved every minute of the stay. Friendliest staff of any hotel.... will bend over backwards for you.

title: Al Manzil Well worth the money!
text: We just returned from a trip to Dubai and stayed at the Al Manzil.Everything about this hotel is perfect.The rooms are well equiped and comfortable.Added touches like a beautiful stationary box and easy access keys make this a Deluxe experience. The breakfast buffet was very nice and the staff were the nicest of any hotel I have stayed in. Concierge service was excellent as was the Housekeeping services.We ar independent travel agents and would definetly recommend this hotel

title: Very nice hotel in new area of Dubai
text: I stayed for five days in this wonderful hotel and enjoyed every minute of it. A very nice hotel with great staff and beautiful rooms. Also, the restaurant is very good and offers a high quality range of Middle Eastern food. The outdoor pool area is perfect and the hotel is centrally located in Old Town behind the Burj Dubai. There is a lot of building construction going on around the hotel, but it never really bothered us. A highly recommended hotel for those, who want to enjoy a couple of days in luxury with out having to take out a mortgage for it. By the way: Make sure and book your room online, which is half price compared to directly through the hotel.

title: The Name Say it all......
text: "Al Manzil" the Arabic word for "Home" where you feel exactly like your at your home,Located in the heart of "Burj Dubai" district just off Sheikh Zaid Rd. & few steps from his sister hotel Qamardeen. Coordinate at N 25 11 30.6E 55 16 40.3A 4 Stars hotel Furnished in Arabic, north African western mixed design.I stayed 3 nights with my wife in a business / leisure tripConstruction around the Hotel a bet disturbing but once its finish will be a great benefit; it is projected to be the modern new expected Dubai down townParking is available under the hotel no worries her.Reception was super fast organized and mot important with a big smileMy room was standard non-smoking room booked by travel agent with a rate of $214 per night including taxes B&B basis.We loved the room so much thought a little space, you will move around easily and every thing is fit perfectlyBreakfast served at the main restaurant "Conservatory" until 10AM and a bit longer on weekends, food is great exceed (quality & variety) what you may get on 5 stars Hotels in DubaiOther restaurant "Courtyard" we liked this out door restaurant so much mainly at night where they have these small electrical candles, great food and Shisha hubbly bubbly for the ones whom like it.Concierge service is out-standing every one want to offer the help and they do it very will especially the Moroccan Staff.To avoid rush ours and "Salik" charges why not to park the car and use the Emirates free shuttle bus (both directions) but remember to be there at reception on time the bus will stop only for few minutesAlso, why not take a peek to the new mall next to hotel and many recreation attractions planned and already just openOver all I found this hotel great for both work and moderate Arabic style leisure and defiantly I will go back again and recommend it to others.?Aboaziz

title: Great for business rubbish for leisure
text: The Al Manzil was nicely decorated having just had a make over - the staff were great and helpful.Rooms were nice though the bath in the bedroom was a bit odd.As it is situated in an area that wont be complete till next year getting a taxi means having to order one or pray someone is being dropped off at the time you want to go out.Its nicely situated between Dubai and Jumeirah so taxi fares are reasonable for Emirates Mall and City Centre.Nice sheeshah bar in the evening that seems to be a local hotspot.

title: Excellent 4 Star Hotel
text: The Staff was wonderful and the services was excellent. Yes I admit the location is really not in the City center however I dint really have to travel much and spent most of my time at the hotel. The Facilities are good and Internet is free everywhere in the hotel and in the rooms. The rooms are nice and since I had requested for a higher Floor I got the room at the 8th Floor which had a Beautiful View Of the old town residential area ( I have posted a few pics and you can have a look at them ). Well the foodHmmmm The food was not bad, but I guess they can make improvements. I should say the Snacks & Desserts Were really good!Among the 4 Star Hotels I have stayed In Dubai , This is the best & Also much better than some 5 star hotels that I have stayed in Dubai!

title: Fabulous
text: From the moment we arrived we were very impressed, the hotel is beautifully designed, with really great rooms (the ability to turn the television round to watch it in the bath located in the centre of the room was definitely a novelty). The staff were extremely helpful - and the buffet breakfast amazing. We also had dinner in the Sports Bar which was extremely good value. Location wise, the hotel isn't the most central - however, the taxis are so cheap we didn't feel it mattered. Once all the building work (which you are not aware of once inside) has been completed around the hotel, it will be a 5* hotel with prices to match, so take advantage now.

title: Good Place
text: Good Hotel,Rooms are clean, staff is very kind, breakfast and bufet may be improved.

title: Loved it
text: We stayed two nights (wished it had been a bit more!) in this gorgeous hotel and it was a delight. The staff were superb in all senses: warm, professional and ready to help at any point. We had our 4 year daughter with us and they were very attentive with her and her needs. Breakfast buffet is fabulous. It is true that it is not so close to the center, but Dubai is pretty spread out, so perhaps it's good to stay one/two nights in Deira and then move out to this hotel. There is a free shuttle service to the beach and to two of the most important malls (Ibn Batuta and Emirates) if you are planning to do some shopping, which is what one does in Dubai (not much more to do after you've seen museums/Gold souk and the like) don't hesitate to enjoy this little jewel of hotel.We got a very good deal booking through [--] Enjoy[--]

title: Wow
text: hFirstly get the construction out of the way, leaving SZR at exit 51 and taking the construction road toward the Burj Dubai, through roads with new builds either side. Not your cup of tea? Ignor it as it is worth the wait.Greeted with a cool drink and frozen hand towel upon registration just comenced what was an idillic week. The reception is peaceful and cool, with staff who are pleasant and appear very genuine. The room was Ab Fab. A bath took centre stage so take your bubble bath and loofa. Views of the Burj Dubai that are second to none.The pool is quiet and although there is a great deal of construction in the area, it was not intrusive.Buffet breakfast is well worth the 70 or so dhs and the evening buffet was excellent the nights that we used it.Booked through hotels.com the hotel was more than affordable, however, this will not last. Once the srea is completed, the tarrif will be at least four times what I paid, so get in while you can.I cannot praise the staff or this hotel enough. Look beyond the construction and go get a unique view of the emerging Burj Dubai.

title: great hotel
text: stayed here for a few days and liked the hotel,great sports bar

title: Excellent value
text: I stayed here for just over a week and wasn't dissapointed. The rooms were modern, clean and had everything you could want. I liked the arabic designs throughout the hotel and the staff were always very helpful. The pool isn't large but certainly big enough to swim. They also have a nice gym and good food restaurants. There is a sports bar and a nice terrace to sit out in in the evenings.The hotel is dead opposite the Burj Dubai, which you can see from the plane, and although there is construction going on as they complete the "old town" it won't disturb you. Good location for Sheik Zayed road and there is a daily shuttle to the beach, malls etc. Good location for business meetings, all in all very pleasant stay.

title: Beautiful
text: I spent five nights at the Al Manzil, and am now completely spoiled. The building is beautiful, rooms are very comfortable and spotless, and the service is the best I can remember at any hotel. The courtyard/bar is perfect, a great place to hang out. Drinks are expensive, but that's the case with just about every hotel bar on the planet. And this level of service for around $130 USD a night is an absolute steal in my opinion.Of course, the big drawback is the massive construction site around the hotel that stretches as far as the eye can see in every direction. I wasn't bothered by noise, but you can't really leave the hotel at all without a taxi. Now, Dubai is by no means a walkable city, so I suppose that's fairly common, but it would have been nice to be able to walk somewhere. On the bright side, taxis are fairly cheap in Dubai.Of course, when all the construction is finished, Al Manzil will have a fantastic location right between the world's tallest building and the largest shopping mall outside of North America. I'm sure that the rates will go through the roof, and justifiably so. But for now, it's a terrific bargain if you're willing to put up with a slightly inconvenient location.

title: Relax in the courtyard
text: I used the reviews in Trip Advisor when choosing this hotel and was not disappointed. Rooms are superb if you like a modern layout. On arrival a cold apple juice and ice-cold towel is accompanied by an Arabic coffee. Nice touch. Pool and fitness centre are clean and pleasant. The bar is lively and the food (S.African influence) is very good. The burger was my best ever. People obviously come from miles around for an evening at this bar or in the courtyard. With a mass of shisha pipes, lush plants, gentle fountains, chill-out music and wonerful staff, this is the place to wind down and spend a few hours. The atmosphere is just right.The staff are so accommodating and genuinely friendly. The only drawback, common to Dubai, is that you can't go for a stroll out of the hotel as it is surrounded by a seriously large building site. One day, when the mall and the tower are complete, this hotel will be out of reach of normal mortals...

title: Loved the breakfast
text: I went along with my family and stayed there for 3 days. We all loved the hotel and comfort provided in the rooms. We liked the indian restaurant and the breakfast as well. Family enjoyed too much and also enjoyed the halloween night during our stay in double decker bar. My sone liked the hotel too much and enjoyed every bit of it.

title: Not 5 star
text: We stayed in a 2 bedroom suite (apartment). These suits are not in the main building, but in a separate building with its own reception etc. Getting to the hotel building and swimming pool etc is only possible via the street.Size of apartments are OK. Nothing special. They are furnished in a very traditional hotel style. No dishwasher in the kitchen. Washing machine available.Maintenance is in the hotel is very poor. We needed 5 times a maintenance guy during our 8 days stay. The hotel pool is missing tiles etc. I am wondering what this place will look like in 2 years...Cleaning staff is very friendly. The reception staff (only speaking about the Suites reception) is absolutely not on 5 star level. You don't feel really as an appreciated guest. Some with the Bell boys: Never during our stay they opened the front door for us: Even not when one of us was struggling to get the baby stroller in.Location is great for shopping lovers: Opposite the Dubai Mall. You can walk to there. At the moment you still need to walk through the dirt, but it looked like the pavements will be finished within the next months. Beach is far away. The Murooj complex includes a 24HR supermarket with home delivery service.Be aware: at the front site of the Suites Building is a lot of traffic. Partly on bridges. Our first room was on the second floor. After the first night we switched rooms because we could hear the cars clearly in our room. For families the hotel is well equipped. Of course the 2, 3 bedroom suites a convenient. The swimming pool is good for children (no slides or something), including an area with just a 5cm deep water, where babies can play in the water.Would I stay here again? Most probably not. There are way better Apartment hotels in Dubai (Marriott Marina or Oasis) which are really 5 star. Service at the Murooj Rotana is not more than you can expect from a 3 star hotel.

title: Just OK
text: We had a week at this hotel. The facilities are good, although hotel guests only get to use two of the three pools. The best and largest pool is reserved for residents, even though there was hardly ever anyone using it while we were there. The service at the front desk was poor, staff not particularly helpful with information and we felt they couldnt be bothered. Cleaning and maid service was great. The private beach is quite a distance from the hotel and you have to pay 165 dh per person to get there using hotel transport so cheaper to call a taxi, tennis is an also extra cost and we didnt see anyone using the courts. Rooms were clean and spacious but wouldnt stay here again, lack of personal service and unfriendly front desk staff.

title: don't like it
text: nice location but the construction in the roads make it messy, the staff not well trained, expensive internet, the cleanliness not that good but it's average

title: Very good !
text: We stayed here during Ramadan (september). The hotel looks very nice. Rooms were modern and clean. Staff was friendly and helpfull (especially the luggage guy). The best thing about this hotel is it's location. 5 Minutes by foot to the Dubai Mall and not far from the Burj Dubai. We visited the Dubai mall just after Iftar so it was very busy. The mall is worth a visit (it has an aquarium,fountains outside and much more). You can also eat something at the mall (cheaper than in the hotel). We had a summer promo 450AED/ROOM which was a rather cheap price for this hotel. I would certainly stay here again for this price however for the normal 2200AED rate I would choose another hotel !

title: Nice stay at the heart of the city
text: Staying at Al Murooj Rotana was a great experience, with its location at the heart of the city and next to dubai mall "world's largest mall" its an ideal option if you'd like to have a break while still being at the city.The room was very luxurios and clean with balcony viewing the pool, the room service is super, they just do things in a record of time.The breakfast was very good, u'll find a variety of tasty and delecious food till 11:00 am, in addition the have a variety of restaurants.what I didnt like about it was just the long time vallet took to get my car " that happened for 3 or 4 times" and the "relatively long" time they took to finalize our check-out and the small lobby which get crowded with russian girls at night.

title: nice hotel personalized service especially in the restaurants
text: many variety of restuarants, the food is verry tasty, especially the italian night at Pergolas restaurant .

title: Great Choice if you want a "Resort" feel....
text: This was a quick "Girls" weekend getaway. While the Rotana family has over 12 hotels in Dubai, I chose this one as from the reviews, it seemed to have a nice "resort" feel. Glad I DID!! Just as others have stated, you were welcomed with smiles and never a bother. I always book "Club Rooms" as I think it's definitely worth the extra cost..ie free internet, afternoon snacks and most importantly "unlimited alcoholic drinks" in the evenings. On one nite, they had a display of Sushi that was just scrumptious (and I don't eat just anyone's Sushi!) One morning we decided to try the breakfast in the main lobby.........uh........no! It was like a circus and had to find someone to just to pour us some coffee. As far as the rooms, they are really nice but SMALL. If you need space, upgrade to a suite. (Unfortunately, for us they were all booked and tried to accomodate us by putting us in an two bedroom apartment) We told them we'd like to "see it" first and then decide. Well.....it's HUGE, but is not as updated in style and decor in its interior as the rest of the hotel. Thanks for trying:-)It's better suited for longer stays. Had a wonderful massage for half price "summer special" and the Club lounge also gave us two free alcoholic drink coupons upon check-in at the "Double Decker" Pub. Had a scumptious lunch at "Zaika" Indian restaurant. Would I stay there again? You BET!!

title: Resot like ambience
text: The approach to the hotel was marred by the construction activity around. However, inside the hotel everything was good. The staff was helpful when I was looking at excursion options. Room service was prompt and within the time limit they mentioned while placing the order.I tried two restaurants and both exceeded my expectations.

title: stylish beautifull hotel a good review from a good critic
text: I stayed in Al Murroj with a friend, it is the third time i have stayed there and certainly not the last, the hotl is beautifull, full of marble and fresh flowers, staff are always there to greet you at the doors, and i never had to wait for a taxi or car.The rooms are very well services, in the morning and in evening for turndown service, the staff always remember me every time i return, which is great.The restaurants are great...although a little expensive....but food is delicious.The only qualm i have is obviously the contruction, once your in the hotel you cant hear it but once outside, it is a bit of an eye sore, it would be nice at some point to talk a walk over to the dubai mall (if they ever build a pedestrian crossing) lol, also nearly everyday i took a taxi to jumeirah beach and it took less than 20 mins in rush hour and cost roughly 30dhs, just make sure the taxi drivers start out the meter on 3dhs as they like to put it higher if ur a tourist.Overall the hotel is great, the next time i return to dubai (next week) i will be staying in Le Meridien not Al Murooj only because of business...if it was pleasure it would be Al Murooj all the way baby lol.ps...i will also write a review on Le Meridien once completed

title: Mixed feelings!
text: My partner and I arrived in Dubai on a midnight flight. We had a four night stay booked on the Club Floor which included limousine pickup. We were looking forward to being welcomed by our limousine pick up however one never arrived. We were told by reception that we never organised a pick up although they could tell me of the flight we were to arrive in on (only mentioned in the email requesting pick up). We were told to catch a cab (30 minute wait in 40 degree heat at 1am) and they would reimburse us which they did. We then arrived at reception to be told yet again that we had not organised a car pick up but mentioned my email. (Contradictions were rife!) My partner and I were then placed in a non smoking room that wreaked of smoke. We were told no other rooms available until the following day. The shower then lost pressure about seven times so needless to say I was at my wits end and ready to find another hotel the following day. We made our way to breakfast on the Club Floor to be greeted by an extremely friendly yet professional young lady. She kindly advised that they had another room for us and that concierge would organise the luggage. We had breakfast and found the young gentleman especially Vyksh (apologise if incorrect spelling) to be wonderful. The service supplied to us by the staff on the 14th floor were outstandng and turned our stay around. The concierge were also all extremely polite and willing to assist with any enquiries we had which made our stay more pleasurable. I can not however say the same about the staff on the main reception in the foyer. We found them rude, non willing to help and did not follow up on issues we had encountered.We were given a complimentary dinner in the Pergolas restaurant for the inconvenience on the first night which we were advised included drinks however our we were billed woth these drinks on our check out. (They hesitantly removed these in the end). We are still awaiting for the refund of the deposit taken from our credit card however if we only dealt with the fantastic staff on the 14th floor we would stay again otherwise definitely not.

title: Nice hotel friendly staff. Pity about the construction around the hotel though...
text: Stayed at the Al Murooj Rotana for 7 nights on business in Dubai. It's a nice 5 star hotel, a 40 dirham taxi ride from the airport. Reception is quite impressive - lots of marble, fountains, chrome etc, and incredibly efficient and friendly staff.I arrived at 00:30 on a Saturday morning, and the downstairs disco was pumping very loud music out, with several people spilling out of the club and onto the driveway up to reception. Not the greatest first impression, but I was put in a room on the 7th floor, so it really didn't bother me in the least.My room was average sized for Dubai (in the UK, it would be huge, but hotels in Dubai all seem to be much larger than their European counterparts), and well appointed, with the usual minibar / plasma TV / phone & TV volume in the bathroom / air con / dressing gown & slippers, and a nice separate desk and comfortable working chair by the window. I overlooked the rear of the hotel, so could see the 4 or 5 separate swimming pools, outside bar, and patio area below.The food was excellent - there are 5 or 6 different restaurants on site, and I ate in the buffet restaurant on a couple of occasions. Lots of choice, vast selections of salads, breads, and desserts, and a central area with a couple of chefs who will happily cook the fresh chicken, steak, and fish available. Lots of kiddie-friendly options too - although I was away on business, I spotted plenty of food that my 8 year old would have happily eaten.The only time I found the bar at the hotel was on my first night - after an 8 hour flight, I fancied a quick beer before hitting the sack, so found the Bus Stop English Pub.... yep, after flying halfway across the world from England, I found that the hotel had an Olde Worlde English pub in the basement! It seemed quite a trendy place to drink, so had very loud music and plasma TVs everywhere showing MTV, but the beer was cold and hit the spot.The only downside to the hotel (and this is a problem with much of Dubai at the moment) is the scale of construction going on all around the hotel. For example, the Dubai Mall is only about 800 metres from the hotel, but standing in between is an 8 lane dual carriageway, plus a construction site, which means that you have to take a 10 minute taxi ride round the oneway system, only to end up a stones throw from where you began! It's also worth noting that construction is worked on 24 hours a day, and although it didn't affect me, I suspect that this was due to my room being on a high floor. A few other reviewers have reported quite a lot of noise on lower floors, so make sure you ask for a high floor when you book!All in all, a good business hotel, and one that I'd stay at again. Only downer was the very expensive internet access (about 12 GBP per day).

title: Nice place good location
text: Stayed on business 3 nights. excellent rooms, attentive service. Breakfast buffet was alright, lunch quite good. Free shuttle service to/from airport worked flawless. A lot of roadwork and construction around the premises makes it feel dusty and secluded. The pool is nice but not outstanding. Gym is OK. Very nice rooms and bathrooms, only thing missing was free WIFI on the rooms.

title: Nice suites for families
text: My family and I (husband, 2 kids of 13 and 10 yeards old) stayed there for 4 nights while we were arranging our last things before moving from Dubai. We had a 2 bedroom suite, it was very good because it came fully equipped and that helped us a lot.The bathroom could be updated and there was no a/c in them, which was not a problem for us because it was winter but during summer it can be very annoying. The room was ok, comfortable bed and enough space.The service is not the best, they take ages to bring something when you ask. I waited nearly 1 hour (after calling 3 times) for tea towels, before that they brought bathrobes and some towels...but that is common in Dubai because people there hardly speak any English. The location was very good before, but with all the construction taking place around the Hotel it can get very difficult to move around. We went to the Dubai Mall (which is opposite the street) and it took us more than 45 minutes to drive back to the Hotel because of the bad signals and the confusion of the streets.Also because of the construction of a main highway in front of the Hotel try to get a room in the highest floors or pool view, because of the noise.We highly recommend More Cafe...we loved it !A good option if you are looking for a family suite but if you want something else there are better and nicer hotels in Dubai.

title: I had a fantastic holiday.
text: Its not always easy to know what to choose or where to go for a holiday. The best way to rely on recommendation and heres mine. I having stayed in many 5 star hotels and can with all honesty to say that Al Murooj Rotana is a true 5 star hotel and absolutely faultless. The location of it is perfect. All facilities and outlets are on a good level. The service of the staff is impeccable. They are very methodical in their manner of working. They are friendly and always keen to help. The staff are really professional. Al Murooj is a very charming hotel, well designed and spotlessly clean. Attention to detail is a theme that runs through everything in the hotel. My room was spacious, comfortable and exceptionally clean. Housekeeping at the hotel is superb. Room Service was great as well. Check in/ check out was perfect.Club Rotana lounge is a very relaxing and nice place. Everything in it is high class and everything is done with all standards. I had a fantastic stay at the hotel and will not hesitate to recommend it to anyone who would like to have an unforgettable holiday

title: Great stay in an amazing City
text: I work for a major internaional airline so we knew that my standards would be high for the accommodation on a mini-break. With Dubai we were also looking at the major problem of there being simply too much choice!! We had decided to visit the city on the basis that it's one of the destinations I have not yet been to as crew and we fancied a bit of shopping (the Dubai Shopping Festival was too tempting an offer for us!!). We were amazed at the volume of 5* hotels and the competitive prices on offer across the city. The Al Murooj Rotana had an offer which meant that it worked out the best price basically - after reading thousands upon thousands of reviews of various hotels on TripAdvisor we just decided that we should go for the cheapest offer for a 5* hotel and hope for the best!!!I was so pleasantly surprised I just can't tell you! The reviews for this hotel seemed completely unfair - most hotels had such a mixture of good and bad reviews that we just decided to ignore them and I'm glad we went with that opinion. I had read comments saying that the staff were unfriendly, facilities not good enough and room service rather useless - but I beg to differ. I must point out that I have been around the block a bit and am clued-up on varying cultures - In case of those who are not aware, and with the greatest respect to the wonderful culture, women in Dubai will not be recognised as, well, relevant??? I have my suspicions that some of the reviews written about any of the hotels in Dubai from dissatisfied customers was possibly due to the way the women are recieved. For example, all of our accommodation, car hire etc was booked by me (the missus), but when trying to sort out the car hire the gentleman serving us was not talking to me (despite it being in my name) but to my other half - the same occurred at the hotel reception. It was funny at times as I was asking questions to staff and they would be answering the question to my other half! This is just the culture - I did not feel uncomfortable, disrespected or maltreated in any way as I respect the fact that this is just the done thing. In the same way, I imagine it's strange for a Muslim woman visiting the UK to have a man look her directly in the eye (seen as disrespectful in their native countries apparently). We found that the staff were so friendly and their attention to details was superb. I stay in 4* hotels around the world on a weekly basis and this hotel was, in my opinion, one of the friendliest and professional I have visited in a long time. The room (we had a non-smoking king room with a balcony) contained everything you would expect - a varied and well-stocked mini-bar (not that I would recommend buying anything from a mini-bar as it's ridiculously expensive!), a good sized bathroom with shower and all the lovely little extras we all need (hairdryer, bathrobe, slippers, shampoo etc) and the room was perfectly lovely - much as any other hotel room is from 4-5* to be frank. The amenities at the hotel were also of a very high standard - the pool and fitness centre were lovely, and the restaurants we visited were very good indeed. We'd particularly recommend the Indian Restaurant and, furthermore, the Amarone on their wine list!!!Before our arrival we had been a little worried about the location of the hotel, being in the middle of the business district, but in fairness it was pretty central to everywhere we wanted to visit (and taxis are very cheap!). There is building work going on all over Dubai but we found that it didn't make a difference to our stay.The one and only small detail I will mention is that we were kept awake one night by a rather noisy room party in the room next to us. This can happen in any hotel and I've had it so many times I can't count (and may have actually been in a few of these said room parties on a few occasions admittedly) so all I will say is that we had a door to adjoin said room to ours for bigger guest parties - it's a bit tricky to soundproof a door so maybe you should check this when you are shown your room!!!We both loved the visit - and, yes, Dubai is a very strange place which people will undoubtedly love or hate! We felt it was like a classy version of Las Vegas! Enjoy your stay!

title: Disaster
text: I had been on a business meeting at Al Murooj my stay at the hotel was disaster firstly when I reached airport there was no airport representative I was asked to go to the airport desk at United car rental at airport where I was provided a car after a long wait when I reached hotel the Doorman was unfriendly he did not greet me there was no bellman to take luggage at reception I found that room was not ready I had to wait for 2 hours to get my room I was very hungry but I was not offered any complimentary juice or cookies.The reception staff was unfriendly the staff was not professional I went to concierge for car booking where baabasaab the concierge gave me car to abu dhabi for AED 350 where same car costs AED 250.Anyways in the room the room menu was too small no options.Housekeeping was good the room was clean.I was upset with my stay bcoz of unfriendly staff specially front desk.I would not advise you to visit this hotel as it is good but no good.

title: A very good business hotel
text: To be honest, I can't imagine why anyone would choose to come to Dubai - it is a place of deep shallowness where the hotels and malls are the main destinations and from the local news the air and waters are as polluted as you might expect from a large commercial city and major building site. It's a kind of hell hole with lipgloss.If you have to come to Dubai for business reasons or en-route to somewhere more interesting then this is a pretty good hotel. Like most places in the main business district, it's in the middle of a construction area at the moment, so it's probably not ideal for anyone who needs to sleep with the windows open. I assume that the price reflects this and will rise as it becomes a relatively low rise haven lost in the skyline.But then - if you want to minimise your contribution to global warming then Dubai would hardly be on your list of eco friendly destinations, although the rapid transit system under construction will help a little, the air conditioning is always going to be essential for most people.I found the design of the hotel to be very acceptable in a place where people rarely say "that's enough gold plating". The rooms are pleasant and the food is good. The staff are very friendly and accommodating. So all in all it is a hotel that is more than fit for purpose if you must come to Dubai.

title: Al Murooj is one of the best in the world
text: Al Murooj is by far one of the best hotels I've stayed at. I am in Dubai about every 2 weeks and try to stay there whenever the rate facilitates it. The service of the staff is remarkable, the remember me, they are professional, any problems are immediately fixed and everyone from the doormen to housekeeping to the managers are wonderful. The Double Decker Pub is a lot of fun to just pop down for a drink and some great music. During one of my stays I had to be rushed to hospital via ambulance and their professional nature during the ordeal and the aftercare from their staff from everything to calls to check on me, special arrangements, complimentary gifts, etc. was remarkable. Honestly, I would put the highest marks on this hotel.

title: Great Stay
text: We stayed 3 nights in a very comfortable and nicely furnished double room - the shower was terrific: just what you need when it's 40+c and unbearably humid outside. The staff were the best thing about the hotel - they couldn't do enough for you. Friendly and extremely efficient, nothing was too much trouble.Food was good - in particular the Indian restaurant attached to the hotel was outstanding. The only down side was that it (and other of restaurants and bars in the hotel) were located outside of the main building and it meant walking through the unbearable heat. Obviously this won't be as much as an issue outside of their hottest summer months.We only have two minor gripes. One day the room didn't get made up in the daytime - only when they came in to turn the beds down at night was it tidied. And they don't provide free internet access for any length of time - so I had to pay a fee for checking in to my flight online, which took 3 minutes.Like the rest of Dubai, there's building going on all around it and you can't walk anywhere (too dangerous because of the traffic), but the hotel can arrange a car with driver within minutes, and it's pretty cheap.

title: Service smiles and a warm welcome
text: Stayed two nights at the Al Murooj Rotana on the way back from Iran, and it was an absolute pleasure. Their service was impeccable, the food out of this world (breakfast and the evening buffet) and the staff went out of their way to look after me. The hotel is conveniently located within a 15 minute drive of the airport, yet near the centre of activities. You do not walk in Dubai in July (it was over 50 Celcius and humid when I was there). I used the hotel's limo service to travel around (free limo to and from the airport was great), and reasonably priced for local journeys. The food at the hotel was sumptuous. I took friends out to dinner in the hotel mid-week and we had a far east feast which featured cuisine from China, Korea, Japan, Indonesia etc. Choice was absolutely great and quality was in keeping with the hotel's high standards.I got a good rate as it was out of season. While I didn't have time to use the facilities (leisure or business) the pool scene outside looked great from the window.Highly recommended for business or leisure.

title: Fantastic
text: My wife and i stayed at the hotel as a 4 day stop over on our way to Mauritous on our honeymoon. On arriving which was 2am we were swiftly taken through checking in and were shown to our lovely room by a very friendly receptionist. The room was faultless and as a fantastic bonus had an outside jacuzzi. Perfect.The city location seemed to me fairly irrelevant in most of Dubia as everywhere has large amounts of building work going on and it is too hot to walk any distance outside anyway (air conditioning all the way). The hotel is business traveller orientated but as a honeymoon city break on the way to our beach holiday it proved ideal. There is even a free shuttle bus for residents to the main malls. I did have one complaint regarding my bill on departure but after speaking to the hotel manager it was rectified quickly. All in all a very pleasant stay.

title: Health Hazard
text: This hotel has nice décor (except for the bathrooms), unfortunately thats about it. I feel obliged to let future unsuspecting guest in on the truth. The service is horrendous, almost all of the staff speak little to no English making the simplest of tasks a nightmare coupled with the blatant resentment towards anyone who can afford to stay there, not to mention the time it takes to receive your request if you manage to get to some understanding. It is rated a 5 star hotel however I think this is reserved only for the lobby and grounds. The restaurants are empty 99% of the time except for the buffet which I am happy to give a 3 star too. If you are looking for a quality hotel you will not find it here so save yourself the anguish and find somewhere else. Even if you do complain it will not get you anywhere as they just dont care and we are not high maintenance by any means we just expected decent service for our money. BUT, I have saved the best till last! I am sitting here writing this at 3am in the morning, unable to sleep because of the traffic noise, which I can live with but not the vibration from the massive construction that is going on outside and the putrid smell of the diesel that fills the whole room making my eyes sting and so nauseous I actually threw up the other night. You wake up in the morning so ill you feel like you have the flu. This is a major health concern and I would strongly advise anyone considering staying here to rethink their plans as I wish I had been warned.

title: I am in love with Al Murooj
text: My wifead I have stayed to the Al Murooj several times between 2006 and 2007. Everytime it was an excellent experience. I really miss the hotel now that we work in the States and don't have anymore business to go to Dubai.

title: Very nice
text: Everything was great. They ask too much for high-speed internet in the hotel room, but the wireless internet is free of charge in the lobby and in the lounge, so everyone seems to hang out in those places in the morning and early evening.

title: For the Bussiness Traveler
text: I stayed at the Al-Murooj Rotanna when I attended a conference in Dubai. Defenitely one of the best hotels I've ever been to. Checkin went smooth - staff was friendly and explained everything - from where breakfast will be etc. Normally you have to ask the staff to get info but not at the Al-Murooj. Rooms was beautiful and comfortable. The location will be great once the new mall is completed which are currently being built opposite the hotel. The reastaurants are great. Only had one problem when the waiter forgot to bring my drinks I've orered. The hotel do not cater for children and therefore I will not recommend it for travellers with children. Otherwise, the hotel is great.Defenitely the best service I've ever received.

title: Lovely hote strange location
text: Booked as a 3 night add-on to a tour of India, this is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed at. We could not fault it in any way, the rooms, breakfast, service, pool area were all excellent. We did not eat in the hotel in the evenings but the buffets looked beautiful if a little expensive at 169 dinars each. The hotel is very close to the Burj Dubai, now the tallest building in the world, so at the moment seems to be in the middle of an enormous building site (although we did not hear any noise), but even when the building is complete the location will still be rather strange, in the centre of a busy multi-lane traffic system. You can't walk anywhere and although taxis are plentiful and cheap and it is only 10-15 minutes to the airport, beach or any of the main malls I think I would choose a lower grade hotel on the beach another time.

title: Let Down By Location
text: First and foremost this is a business hotel so I would not recommend that you stay here for a holiday. There are holiday amenities such as a swimming pool and various restaurants around the resort but my impression was that these are more tailored to the other inhabitants of the Rotana Hotels & Suites guests  i.e. the Suites - that makes up 90% of the property.Bearing that in mind I will review this hotel as a business hotel and for what it offered me personally as a business traveller.LocationLocation wise the hotel is unfortunately surrounded by building sites and at the furthest end of the road that leads to the financial centre of Dubai. This made it nigh on impossible to walk into or back from work. This was particularly an issue in the evening when there was a very distinct lack of Taxis around town. Walking back to the hotel is particularly hazardous due to the lack of pavements and the amount of construction going on around you.Dubai is expanding greatly and the hotel can not be blamed for the safety or condition of roads or pavements or indeed for the lack of taxis around town (I later discovered that all the taxis are parked up at the Mall of the Emirates waiting for better fares!!). But personally given the choice again I would ensure I was staying in a hotel much closer to the centre i.e. within safe walking distance from the office. Should I return to Dubai as a tourist rather than on business I would stay in the beach area.StaffAll of the staff were very nice. All very happy, attentive and efficient. The only issue I did have was that we booked an excursion through the concierge and during the evening of the excursion I discovered that we had paid twice as much as other clients on the excursion. I can understand the hotel making a small commission on the booking but a 100% mark up seemed excessive and slightly greedy. I am unsure if this is a hotel policy or just the individual chancing his arm. I would suggest you think twice before booking through the concierge as opposed to booking directly with the operator of the tour.  This applies to any hotel you stay in I am sure!RoomThe room was very comfortable, well furnished and had everything I needed, except an iron and ironing board which were delivered on request.The mini bar was well stocked and slightly on the expensive side  But what business hotel isnt??I had a problem on the first two days of my stay with the water pressure. It coughed and spluttered a bit the first day but the second morning I found myself of being in the position of standing stark naked in the shower covered in soap and the water stopping!! Five minutes later I was starting to panic and contemplating having to wash off using (expensive and refrigerated - brrrrr!) bottled water. Fortunately it spluttered to life again before it came to that, but it was a close call!!I was on the 12th floor and I notice that one of the first people to write a TA review of this hotel had a similar problem on this floor. Probably one to avoid should you be staying here. Having said that the rest of my week there was problem free.FoodI ate breakfast and had only one evening meal at the hotel. All of these were in the main restaurant Pergola.The breakfast was a buffet with a choice of hot and cold breakfast items with a chef to prepare omelettes or eggs. Most of these items were OK but the occasional thing, a pastry here, a yoghurt there was a bit stale or poorly prepared. I have had better breakfasts and buffets at 4* hotels so this being a 5* I was disappointed. On two occasion I asked for eggs over easy but I must have been misheard as on both time I was given eggs over cooked!! If your chef cant cook a couple of fried eggs your restaurant is in trouble!!The evening meal I had was the Italian Buffet. There are various theme buffets throughout the week and judging by the amount of local ex pats that turn up they are obviously popular. I have to say that the food I had was all very nice and with free drink (beer or wine) I can see why its popular! I would go again and would probably try the other nights too based on the quality of the one I did attend.There are four other restaurants around the resort and if they are as good as Pergola was that evening I would not hesitate to try them.SummarySo in summary this is a nice hotel, in a city of very good hotels. Does it deserve 5*? Probably not in comparison to other 5* hotels in the area. It is a good 4* let down by its location (at the moment) and the occasional hiccup.Would I stay there again? Probably not. Maybe in a few years when the immediate area has finished being developed

title: Good hotel but expensive
text: Business hotel, well connected by roads, etc....Good gym and pool, however be prepared to pay through the nose here.

title: Business hotel
text: We spent 3 nights at the hotel and never really felt comfortable. It's probabely more a business hotel, but if you are on vacation, I would recomend staying at one of the beach resorts. There was a big construction right in front of the hotel, but than again, that's Dubai. We got special check-in at the executive floor where they also serve free drinks from 7pm - 9pm,. We appriciated that. The rooms are ok, a bit unpersonal though, and so is the staff. Over all it is a good hotel, located in the center of Dubai but if you are on vacation, go to the beach!

title: Would not stay again
text: We stayed in this hotel for three days on our way out to Mauritius for our honeymoon, the hotel was aware this was our honeymoon but made no effort to make it feel special, unlike the Hilton in Mauritius.We had booked a non-smoking room but there were none available at the time of check in and as we had just had a 8 hour overnight flight, we didnt want to wait around for another to become available, all we wanted to do was sleep. This is a business hotel I would not recommend it for families or for a romantic getaway. I suppose we were disappointed as it was part of our honeymoon and there was no atmosphere in the hotel, mainly business men.There was also a scent in the lobby when you came through the doors which I think was supposed to smell nice!! It was very overpowering and sickly.I love Dubai as I worked over there for a while there is so much to do, I should have gone with the hotels I know, we just wanted to try somewhere different.

title: Absolutely Fabulous!
text: I stayed at Al Murooj Rotana in dec 2006....me and a friend were to stay in dubai for 2 weeks...The best thing about the hotel is their staff....on the first day ...my friend left her passport and ticket in the cab, and the staff were very helpful in helping us find it....Also the rooms are impeccable and leave you nothing to complain about.... the water is always replenished.....and the room always looks fresh and new.....The only thing that did not please me very much was the in - room dining menu. It is very limited and after a few days you are ordering the same food every night. My suggestion would be to try out the different restaurants at the hotel....or explore what the city has to offer..!!The hotel is very close to all the biggest shopping malls...and restaurants which is a big plus for this place!All in all.... my stay there was very nice and unforgettable!!! Dubai is a lovely city and this hotel made all the difference!

title: Not for a holiday!
text: I stayed here shortly after it's opening in March 2006.It is the only hotel from which I have demanded to be relocated. It was booked late from the UK and it seemed like a good holiday choice but beware... Avoid if you are going to Dubai for a beach type holiday. The location is between a motorway intersection, apartment complexes and some urban scrub land looking strangely like a camel farm. It is at least 15 minutes' drive to the beach due to a combination of heavy traffic and roadworks (and there is a substantial cost for access to a very indifferent beach when you get there). Forget about walking, pavements don't exist. You are totally stranded in this bizarre pseudo luxury bubble which is only good if you are here on business and going everywhere by car. The rooms are fine with nice facilities. Only a small pool was available and the grounds were the public areas of some apartment blocks nearby. The bar/nightclub is a dreadful mock London pub with no atmosphere and surly door staff despite being totally empty. The reception staff became grumpy at the suggestion that all was not as had been advertised. I got on the phone to get us relocated to the nearest Hilton on Jumeirah beach which was a great improvement. Having said that, Dubai is dreadfully overrated and this is what happens when you ask someone to book a holiday for you. If you have been to 5 star hotels before, the shiny lobby won't be enough to impress.

title: Our favourite 5 star hotel
text: This was our second time at the Al Murooj and we were suitably impressed yet again.We have stayed in several 5 star hotels across the US, Europe and China. This definately ranks up there with the best. The staff are very friendly, the hotel is immaculate, the rooms are spacious and the food is superb.If you are a beach addict you might prefer one of the beach front hotels. But if like us you enjoy exploring the area then the Al Murooj is perfect.We will definately be using this hotel again when we next go back to Dubai.Recommended.

title: gr8 holiday
text: A very happly couple Just returned from a 10 night stay in the Al Murooj Rotana in Dubai. This is classed as a 5 star but I would give it a 5star + + + The hotel was extremely clean and very comfortable with the room being turned down twice a day and setting out bedroom slippers a the side of the bed at night.The room also has a minibar & digital safe. There was lot of building work going on but we found this amazing to see and glad we didnt miss the views in the city area as we where just off the main highway. It is only a short taxi ride from everywhere very cheap. Make sure and get up for the buffet breakfast, excellent choice of food, don't miss the double decker pub for good atmosphere. The dj became a very good friend and also enjoyed a few trips with us as he was class a VIP, Supermarket to rear of complex is open 24 hrs and stock's all main brands of english food and drink eg walkers crips :-) starbucks is at the side of the hotel also.The weather was 47 'c most days and just what we need.i would book this hotel again.

title: enjoyable stay
text: Being a first time visitor to Dubai we did a fair bit of research on a hotel to stay. We wasnt disappointed with this hotel, a lot of our friends stayed in the beach area, as we wasnt worried due to not being able to sit in the sun for long hours, this hotel was a great location. A high standard service, room was very clean. A lot of building going on but we found this amazing to see and glad we didnt miss the city views. We were given our room an hour after arriving sleepy at 7am following a night flight, which was appreciated as check in isnt until late afternoon. We had pool view. Nice buffet breakfast, excellent choice of food, soya milk was provided which was welcome as I have a dairy intolerance. Good choice of resturants, double decker was a good pub atmosphere, the seafood resturant was our treat. We enjoyed being away from the tourist side of things, as the hotel really was occupied by lot of business clients, which made it pleasant and pool area quiet. Good access to shopping by taxis which were always available. Supermarket to rear of complex open 24 hrs and starbucks. Good hotel for couples.My only moan was reception staff didnt always give you full attention, eg answering the phones when we were being dealt with as a customer.

title: Fabulous stay at the Al Murooj
text: I stayed at the Al Murooj Rotana in Dubai in April of this year with my sister and daughter. We were delighted on arrival to be upgraded to a Club room free of charge. The hotel itself was extremely clean and the rooms very comfortable. We found the staff to be very attentive. Nothing was too much trouble from arranging taxis to booking trips. Others have complained that the hotel caters mainly for business guests but we found quite the opposite in that they had a good knowledge of places to visit, eat and trips to take. We cannot fault the staff in any way. We dined in the hotel on a couple of occasions and found the food to be of a very good standard. We had a thoroughly enjoyable stay in Dubai and felt this was enhanced by our choice of hotel. I would have no hesitation in recommending the Al Murooj Rotana to anyone wanting to see the sights of Dubai. If it is a beach holiday you are looking for, then you may be better advised to stay at one of the beachfront hotels, but if you are looking to see the sights of Dubai then I don't think you could do better than the Al Murooj for location and price.

title: Very clean and friendly
text: Just returned from a 6 night stay in Dubai. Our travel agent found us this hotel as we wanted a room where our 18year old daughter could stay with us. This is classed as a 5 star but I would give it a 5star + + +.It is in the city area just off the main highway a short taxi ride from everywhere. The food in the restraunts was fab. As was the service at the pool. If you can try to upgrade to a club suite (extra benefits are well worth it)

title: Average
text: We had booked a club room having done so in other hotels, including the Grand Hyatt in Dubai, but found the Club Rotana rooms to be below our expectations.After a superb overnight flight with BA we arrived at the hotel early and were taken to the club lounge for check in, as expected the room was not ready but after a leisurely breakfast we were told it had been cleaned. We were a little suprised that our room was on the 3rd floor bearing in mind that the lounge was on the 14th and we expected club rooms to be in a similar vacinity and when we arrived at the room we were convinced that it was only a standard room. It was very small with a small bathroom where the shower was over the bath not in a separate cubicle as we would have expected. After falling asleep we woke later to find our suitcases had not arrived at which point we went back to the lounge to complain. We were told the room was a standard but with club privaledges and infact club rooms were identical but just on a higher floor. We spent the night in a room on the 8th floor and the following day they transferred us to a suite on the 3rd, which was nicer but in reality only the same size and spec as we were expecting a club room to be.On the whole I would say that for the size of the complex everything to do with the hotel itself is small; the rooms, the lobby, the club lounge, the pool. In essence an average stay at an averge hotel although the canapes in the lounge were very nice!!Eat at the Latino restaurant and the Indian restaurant - food ok both very expensive.Not a terrible stay but the next time we go to Dubai we will not be staying here

title: Could do better
text: Whilst we'd read mixed reviews we were not put off by local construction work (after all, Dubai is undergoing an amazing transformation) and were delighted to have a view overlooking the Burj Towers site, how wonderful to see what a difference a year makes in this great city !!!!!Our room was lovely, we'd upgraded to a club floor to enjoy the benefits this afforded us but in all honesty, unless you're a business traveller (in which case it's a great investment) the only benefit was the room, we had to wait for tables in the lounge and the breakfast offering was only ok. However, the room was very spacious, spotless, big bathroom featuring elemis products (always a bonus). Little things count though in a 5 star hotel, and we were constantly comparing this hotel to the Hilton Dubai Creek in which we'd stayed last year (and, it has to be said, we were blown away by the place!). Our morning paper didn't arrive and yet although we'd told our concierge this, we were still charged for it. The concierge team really had very little local knowledge, in fact several members of the staff directed us to Crystal C bar in the hotel on the night it was closed, a wasted half an hour traipsing round the complex!!!! This hotel has tremendous potential to rival some of the other 5 star hotels in Dubai, the views alone are astounding. But lets not forget, Dubai does 5 stars exceptionally well and so the Al Murooj has to raise its game. I feel that the hotel is a sideline for the whole complex, guests are not treated in any way special and that for me was the disappointment, after all, in Dubai that's what we expected following our previous visit.When checking out, we were treated appallingly by the front desk who wrangled over a tub of cashew nuts we hadn't had and adopted a very effective shoulder shrugging technique which did not go down well with my husband at 7am. A fellow guest waiting to check in was left to stand unattended at the front desk for 10 minutes before anyone even acknowledged his presence.It's also worth mentioning that we visited to attend the Dubai World Cup and although many guests there were also attending, the hotel had decided not to offer a courtesy shuttle bus, something many other hotels had provided for their guests.So, in summary, a great hotel for business travellers located midway on the Sheikh Zayed Road. Leisure travellers, well, I believe you can find a hotel that would better suit your needs.

title: Stayed a sum total of 3 hrs!
text: We booked this hotel as part of a stopover deal with an airline - we were promised a beautiful & newly opened hotel and we were soooo disappointed. Having travelled all over the Middle East, this hotel just didn't live up to the normal 5* standards of Dubai and it was more of a business hotel than anything else.The lobby wasn't the sort of place you could relax and the room was tiny with cheap furniture, small beds, and a lovely view of the road. On top of this the swimming pool was out of order - apparently there was construction going on next door and they'd damaged a pipe which had consequently drained the pool. We were in Dubai for a relaxing break where the pool was to be our focus!!!!! When you look at the website or in a brochure, the pool complex looks massive but this is NOT RIGHT - 75% of the grounds is for residents of the surrounding apartments and all the hotel guests get is a smallish pool. When we queried about the out of order pool they said it would take at least a few days to be sorted and we were only there for 5 - they wouldn't let us use the apartment pools and suggested we used the splash pool around the side of the hotel- now that sounds fine but understand that you had to get on a golf cart for a ten minute journey in 42 degrees- right next to the main road - and then walk for another 5 or 10 minutes before getting to what could only be described as a paddling pool with about 5 chairs....and no one could see our problem!!!!!!!!!! Oh and it was Ramadan so if we wanted a drink we had to endure the 10 minute walk, the 10 minute golf cart ride and then a walk through the lobby in our pool clothes to go back up to our rooms before doing the return journey back to the pool - convenient i think not.So funnily enough we checked out and moved to a far nicer hotel with beautiful grounds and a pool you could actually swim in and a pool you were allowed to drink water around despite it being Ramadan.Avoid!

title: First class all the way
text: My husband and I stayed at this hotel on the recommendation of our travel agent. It was fantastic, the service, the food, our room and the hotel were all fantastic. The staff cannot do enough to make sure that you have a great time and are well looked after. The rooftop pool is a great way to cool off in the very high temperatures. The variety of food is incredible and we will be returning again (hopefully) later this year. Five star plus, thoroughly recommend.

title: Luxurious Hotel
text: We spent 4 nights ant the Al Murooj after 7 nights at Hilton RAK which was all inclusive. All booked through Virgin holidays. We love Dubai and this was our 3rd trip. The hotel was fantasric. Great breakfast and lunch but we found the 2 exclusive restaurants near the pool terrbly expensive, which is probably why they were empty every night. The Double Decker pub had a great atmoshere and very good wholesome food. The pool was lovely just a shame about the weather. It rained for 36hrs solid very unlike Dubai!! As it was Dec we lost the sun early due to high rise buildings around us but this did hide the cranes which are everywhere, but it didn't bother us and it wasn't noisy just didn't look nice! We much prefered the Beach Club which was a 10 min courtesy bus ride away. Lovely beach and the pools were heated-lovely. THe hotel location is great. Near to Mall of the Emerates & Ski Dubai nad also near to the city. Cabs were very cheap and plenty of them. I would stay here again as it was good value for money. Do ask for a view overlooking the pool though unless you prefer a building site!

title: Excellent Stay
text: Booked this hotel through 'greatest hotels in the world site' and had special offer 4 nights double room for £400 approx including taxes which isn't bad for 5 star in dubai. Great location central to shopping and easy access to the beach. Rooms were nice and spacious. Pool area was lovely although access was through restaurant there were toilets and changing facilities outside. Outside bar and snacks were nice and pool attendants were efficient bringing towels and laying them on loungers of your choice, bringing cold flannels and strawberries and melon round was nice touch. Guests seemed to be mainly business customers which did not bother us and staff were very friendly and helpful. Main buffet restaurant was nice on evening paying one price per head for all you can eat and inclusive of wine and beer which is good value of equiv of about £15 per head and half price for kids. Went into Double Decker pub attached to the hotel which seemed full of ex-pats middle aged simon cowell look-alikes and kids could only go in in the afternoon (after 6pm had to leave). My only critical remark about the hotel was when checking in we asked for a late evening check out at 6pm as we had a late flight back. The receptionist said the hotel was full and we would have to pay full room rate for an extra day. I declined then on last day decided to ask again and they said half day room rate which I agreed. So I would suggest to ask a few times to try to get price down. The hotel also offered a beach transfer to the Dubai Marine beach hotel at an extra cost which was ok (no where near as good as Jumeria beach club or hilton beach which is where we visited previous years).Thoroughly enjoyed holiday and would definately recommend this hotel if travelling to Dubai.

title: Truly superblocation...servicecomfort
text: This was not our first visit to Dubai and we have stayed in several hotels including the sister Jumeirah Beach hotel which we loved. However the Al Qasr at Madinat Jumeirah has a more traditional Arabic décor and ambience. From the minute we arrived the staff could not do enough for us and considering the hotel was full because of the half term school holidays we still had prompt attentive service. A welcome drink and face towels were supplied with a smile as we sat on a couch to check in. We arrived early morning after an overnight flight and as our bedroom would not be ready until the afternoon we were shown to a comfy lounge with shower facilities and changing rooms. Once changed we went down to breakfast with an amazing choice of good high quality food on offer. The waitress service was prompt in offering you tea or coffee then you could help yourself to the endless array of fresh fruit, yoghurts, breads, porridge, or any variation of cooked breakfast with the eggs cooked freshly to your choice. By 11.00 I had a message on my mobile phone to say the room was now in fact ready and our luggage would be taken up for us. The bedroom was spacious very comfortable well decorated and spotlessly clean. The bath room was large with separate shower and bath and His and Hers toiletries. A veranda with chairs had a view over the front entrance were all the Rolls Royce, Ferraris, Bentleys and other expensive cars were parked. The hotel has numerous restaurants too many to mention but I would recommend you book a table early in your stay to avoid disappointment as many were full during our stay. There is a nice safe beach adjoining the hotel and the Wild Wadi Water Adventure Park (where hotels guest get free admission) is minuets away by the courtesy golf cart.A great way to see the hotel grounds and to get to some of the restaurants is to use the Abras the small taxi boats that sail around the hotels waterways.All in all this is a fabulous hotel with charming friendly staff and great facilities we cant wait to return on our next visit to Dubai

title: Nice hotel minor points to get it to true 5*
text: My husband and I stayed at the Al Qasr during the second leg of our honeymoon (first being in the Maldives - true luxury!) Overall, we had a lovely stay in this hotel however in our opinion, it did not quite live up to the expectation of luxury that it sells itself on. I did a lot of research prior to booking this hotel and do not regret it, perhaps i would have stayed at the Mina instead as the Al Qasr was full of Russian families as it must have accepted a number of package holiday bookings. On the plus side, it is huge, part of the Madinat resort which is great in terms of location and things to do. It has plenty of restaurant choices, souks for shopping, a great bar (try to get the table on the balcony which looks on to the Burj) and a great afternoon tea place which appeared to be favoured more by locals than tourists.Downsides were breaksfast (great choice but given full occupancy of the hotel, felt like a cattle farm), the size of the place (this place is vast, you need buggys and little boats to transport you around so you need to plan things like going to the beach as it could take up to 15mins to get there from your room), service was not quite on par with true 5* (we had a problem with our shower, this was reported on the first night, the next day and then again the following day to the duty manager before an engineer came to have a look, all the time we had to have a bath and were not adequately compensated). The other disappointment was the room, we had an Arabian Deluxe which was relatively small and the shower was opposite the toilet with only a shower curtain partition, not quite what I expect from a 5* hotel.Overall, it was a good hotel but in my experience, not quite what I would have expected given the amount they charge per room. We went to a few of the other hotels in Dubai and they are all luxurious, all huge and all have similar facilities. The Madinat is a great location and for that I would choose to stay here again, but would probably stay at the Mina instead.

title: al qasr is the palace and you are indeed treated as a king
text: Already 5 years we stay once or even twice a year at the Al Qasr hotel. The Al Qasr is part of the Madinat Jumeirah complex which is set up in Arabian Style with the two hotels MinaSalam and Al Qasr and the Souk shopping centre with very nice restaurants along the waterside. The third hotel is the Dar al Masyaf which are the villas set around the gardens and along the beach. The Madinat Jumeirah is located next to the Burj Al Arab.The Al Qasr Hotel is a five star de luxe hotel which derserves the 5 star easily. Everything is organized perfectly and if you choose the premium leisure club you get a separate lounge with playstation and kids playroom while you can enjoy the afternoon snacks and free drinks. Nothing is left to chance at Al Qasr , you can enjoy a very individual service , the staff is always ready to take care of you.
